title: A structural accessibility principle for LbuCas13a activation by noncontiguous DNA.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed every supplementary link on the PubMed Central (PMC) page: there is exactly one, a single PDF (gkag740_supplemental_file.pdf). No spreadsheet, no comma-separated values (CSV) file, no archive. A HEAD request on that PDF returned HTML, not a PDF (PMC /bin/ downloads are blocked), and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out. The paper's own data availability statement, retrieved in full, deposits nothing: 'the data underlying this article are available in the article and in its online supplementary material'. Searches for accession numbers across the whole text, Europe PMC text-mined accessions, NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample/dbGaP) and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI all returned empty. I read the whole open-access full text (94 KB) and counted the experimental units from the Results and Methods.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All counts come from the full text, not from files: 9 groups of noncontiguous DNA targets (G22-6 through G6-22) x 3 design strategies = ~27 target constructs plus a contiguous T28 control; a single-nucleotide mismatch panel at positions 4-28 in two configurations; 27 postoperative glioma tissue samples; 77 serum samples (47 breast cancer, 30 healthy donors). The numeric trans-cleavage (cutting of a nearby reporter molecule) measurements themselves exist only as plotted curves and gel photographs inside figures.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset is deposited anywhere. The only supplementary artifact is one PDF, and I could not retrieve even that (PMC /bin/ path blocked, Europe PMC supplementaryFiles timed out). A PDF of figures and oligonucleotide sequence tables is not a downloadable dataset.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The thing a model would predict (trans-cleavage rate or activation strength) is never a column. It lives as fluorescence-versus-time curves and gel band intensities inside figure panels, so it would have to be constructed by digitizing plots pixel by pixel.

a3_inputs_present.note: The DNA and RNA sequences are in Supplementary Table S1, which is inside the single PDF I could not open. Sequences in a PDF table of ~30 oligonucleotides are transcribable by hand but are not present as machine-readable input.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated carefully in the text (nM concentrations, apparent second-order rate constants near 1e5 M-1 s-1, fluorescence read every 20 s). Units are the one thing this paper does well.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted from the full text: ~27 noncontiguous DNA designs (9 length groups x 3 strategies) plus one contiguous control. The clinical arms are 27 glioma tissues and 77 sera. Every unit count is one to two orders of magnitude below the ~400-row floor for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: One PDF. Size is never the problem here; there is almost no data at all.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked either way, because there is no download to compare the paper against. That is itself the finding.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurement is a genuine physical one, a fluorescence-quencher reporter read on a microplate reader, not another model's output. Provenance is clean; availability is not.

existing_models.name: TIGER (a convolutional neural network predicting CRISPR-Cas13d guide RNA on- and off-target activity, Nature Biotechnology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on ~200,000 measured guide RNAs in human cells; reported to outperform earlier Cas13 on-target design tools, evaluated on held-out guides and transcripts (exact split read from the abstract and news coverage, not from the paper's tables).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Off-target prediction for RNA-targeting CRISPR systems was described as previously unavailable; mismatch-driven partial knockdown was the frontier they opened.

existing_models.name: DeepCas13 (deep learning on guide sequence plus predicted secondary structure, Nature Communications 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Built on >127,000 measured RfxCas13d guides; reported to beat prior methods for guides against both protein-coding and non-coding RNA targets.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which sequence motifs and secondary-structure features drive high efficiency, and transfer across Cas13 orthologs.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a DNA language model such as DNABERT-2 would be the natural fit for short nucleic-acid designs
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be ample, but there is nothing to fit: ~27 labelled designs is far fewer examples than a frozen embedding has dimensions.
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive; irrelevant here because the data does not exist.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. The Cas13d guide-efficiency datasets behind TIGER (~200,000 guides) and DeepCas13 (~127,000 guides) measure a different enzyme (Cas13d versus LbuCas13a), a different substrate (RNA targets versus noncontiguous DNA) and a different readout (gene knockdown versus in vitro reporter cleavage).
integration.join_key: No shared identifier. This paper's constructs are bespoke synthetic oligonucleotides with in-house names (a14_o8, b14_i8, G14-14), not accessions.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: there is no key on which to join, so any combination would be decoration.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own internal control is good biology (contiguous target T28 must activate; Strategy III bare duplexes must not), but with ~27 designs it is a control for a bench experiment, not for a model.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: None. The structural accessibility rule for LbuCas13a plus noncontiguous DNA is measured only in this paper; no second lab, database or assay reports it.

honest_claim_h3: With these files, no model claim is possible at all: the strongest honest statement would be 'a rule inferred from ~27 hand-designed oligonucleotide constructs in one lab, read off figure plots', which is a mechanistic observation and not a prediction task.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the layout of a split DNA target to predict whether it switches on a CRISPR enzyme's cutting activity.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model would see: the two short DNA strands' sequences plus where their overhanging ends sit relative to the guide RNA. Verified count of such designs in the paper: about 27 (9 segment-length groups x 3 layout strategies).
plain_idea.predict: How strongly the enzyme LbuCas13a is switched on, i.e. its rate of chopping up a nearby fluorescent reporter molecule, measured on a microplate reader. That number exists only as curves drawn in the paper's figures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building CRISPR-based diagnostic tests choose these target layouts by trial and error, so a rule would save bench time. But the honest lesson here is the opposite one: the dataset is far too small for a model, and the paper already states the rule in words.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes ~27 designs read from figures; the two existing Cas13 models were trained on ~200,000 and ~127,000 measured guides respectively. We would be four orders of magnitude smaller.

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist per design but are reported as error bars in figures, not as numbers, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated from anything retrievable.

models_beatable.why: TIGER (2023) and DeepCas13 (2023) are recent deep-learning models on six-figure measured datasets; nothing in this paper could be trained well enough to compare, and they address a different enzyme and substrate anyway.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: no join key to the existing models' data, a different enzyme and readout, no shared evaluation split, and no retrievable table on our side to add.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict LbuCas13a trans-cleavage activation strength from the geometry of a noncontiguous (split) DNA target, i.e. from the two complementary segment lengths and the position and length of their overhangs. The paper itself reduces the answer to a stated three-way rule (outer overhangs near the guide's repeat-adjacent side activate strongly, distal outer overhangs weakly, inner overhangs not at all), which a lookup table or a single-feature threshold captures entirely, so machine learning adds nothing even if the numbers were available.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful: the only path to numbers is manually digitizing fluorescence curves out of figure images, which is hours of error-prone human work for a few dozen points, not a pipeline.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the supplementary files. One PDF and no repository accession anywhere in the text, Europe PMC annotations, NCBI links or Zenodo/Dryad kills it in two minutes.

verdict_reason: No deposited data at all: the sole supplement is one PDF (which I could not even retrieve), the measurements exist only as curves inside figures, and the experiment comprises roughly 27 designed DNA constructs, 27 tissues and 77 sera. A1, A2, A3 and A5 all fail. It is a well-executed mechanistic biochemistry and diagnostics paper whose conclusion is a three-case rule stated in one sentence; a lookup table, not a model.
